questions.stem: Calculate the mass of $100$ molecules of oxygen in amu and in grams.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Mass of one molecule
The molecular mass of $\mathrm{O_2}$ is $2 \times 16 = 32$ u, so one molecule has a mass of $32$ u.
Step 2: Mass of 100 molecules in u
$$100 \times 32\ \mathrm{u} = 3200\ \mathrm{u}$$
Step 3: Convert to grams
Use $1\ \mathrm{u} = 1.66 \times 10^{-24}$ g.
$$3200 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-24} = 5.31 \times 10^{-21}\ \mathrm{g}$$
Step 4: Check options
Option (A) gives $3200$ u and $5.314 \times 10^{-21}$ g. Options (B) to (D) use wrong masses ($1600$, $32$, $8$ u), so they fail.
Final Answer:
The mass is $3200$ u or $5.314 \times 10^{-21}$ g, option (A).
(A)
Quick Tip: One $\mathrm{O_2}$ molecule weighs $32$ u and $1\ \mathrm{u} = 1.66 \times 10^{-24}$ g.

questions.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I (Element) | List II (Number of Neutron)
(A) $^{24}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$ | (I) $5$
(B) $^{27}_{13}\mathrm{Al}$ | (II) $12$
(C) $^{9}_{4}\mathrm{Be}$ | (III) $6$
(D) $^{12}_{6}\mathrm{C}$ | (IV) $14$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Step 1: State the rule
Number of neutrons $= A - Z$, where $A$ is the mass number (top) and $Z$ is the atomic number (bottom).
Step 2: Calculate each
(A) Mg: $24 - 12 = 12$, which is (II).
(B) Al: $27 - 13 = 14$, which is (IV).
(C) Be: $9 - 4 = 5$, which is (I).
(D) C: $12 - 6 = 6$, which is (III).
Step 3: Match with options
The pairing is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which is option (B). The other options pair at least one element with a wrong neutron count.
Final Answer:
The matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, option (B).
(B)
Quick Tip: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number.

questions.stem: Which of the following hydrides of Group $16$ elements has highest reducing property?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the trend
The hydrides of group 16 are $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{H_2Se}$ and $\mathrm{H_2Te}$. A reducing agent donates hydrogen or electrons.
Step 2: Link bond strength to reduction
Down the group, the size of the central atom grows and the E-H bond becomes longer and weaker.
A weaker bond breaks more easily, so the hydride reduces more strongly.
Step 3: Conclude
The order of reducing power is $\mathrm{H_2O} < \mathrm{H_2S} < \mathrm{H_2Se} < \mathrm{H_2Te}$. So $\mathrm{H_2Te}$ is the strongest, option (D).
Final Answer:
$\mathrm{H_2Te}$ has the weakest bond and is the best reducing agent, option (D).
(D) $\mathrm{H_2Te}$
Quick Tip: Going down the group, the H-E bond gets weaker, so the hydride gives up hydrogen more easily.

questions.stem: Identify the shape of $\mathrm{IF_5}$ molecule from the following options.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Count electron pairs on iodine
Iodine has $7$ valence electrons. Five are used in bonds with fluorine, leaving $2$ electrons, which is one lone pair.
So there are $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair, $6$ pairs in total.
Step 2: Find the geometry
Six electron pairs give an octahedral arrangement ($sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridisation).
The lone pair takes one octahedral position, leaving five atoms in a square pyramid shape.
Step 3: Other options
Trigonal bipyramidal needs $5$ pairs in all. Square planar is the shape of $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ ($4$ bonds, $2$ lone pairs). Hexagonal does not occur for such molecules.
Final Answer:
$\mathrm{IF_5}$ is square pyramidal, option (D).
(D) Square pyramidal
Quick Tip: Count bond pairs and lone pairs on iodine: $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair.

questions.stem: According to the kinetic molecular theory of gases, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules:
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the result
For gas molecules the average kinetic energy is $\bar{E}_k = \frac{3}{2}k_B T$ per molecule.
It depends only on the absolute temperature.
Step 2: Check each option
(A) Pressure can rise with no change in $T$, so $\bar{E}_k$ does not depend on it.
(B) Volume changes do not alter $\bar{E}_k$ at fixed $T$.
(C) $\bar{E}_k \propto T$, which is true.
(D) Volume has no role. The kinetic energy is the same for all gases at the same temperature, not at the same volume.
Final Answer:
Option (C) is correct.
(C)
Quick Tip: In kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy depends only on temperature.

options.text: Is directly proportional to the absolute temperature
Is the same for all gases at the same volume

questions.stem:
Calculate the enthalpy change for the following reaction, using given bond energy (kJ/mol)
(C-H = 414, H-O = 463, H-Cl = 431, C-Cl = 326 and C-O = 335)
$\mathrm{CH_3OH_{(g)} + HCl_{(g)} \rightarrow CH_3Cl_{(g)} + H_2O_{(g)}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the rule
$\Delta H = \sum(\text{bond energies of reactants}) - \sum(\text{bond energies of products})$.
Step 2: Bonds broken
In $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$ we break one C-O bond ($335$) and one O-H bond ($463$). In HCl we break H-Cl ($431$).
$$335 + 463 + 431 = 1229\ \mathrm{kJ}$$
Step 3: Bonds formed
In $\mathrm{CH_3Cl}$ we form one C-Cl bond ($326$). In $\mathrm{H_2O}$ we form two O-H bonds ($2 \times 463 = 926$).
$$326 + 926 = 1252\ \mathrm{kJ}$$
Step 4: Compute
$$\Delta H = 1229 - 1252 = -23\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$$
The C-H bonds are unchanged and cancel.
Final Answer:
$\Delta H = -23\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, option (A).
(A) $-23\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: $\Delta H$ = bonds broken $-$ bonds formed. Remember water has two O-H bonds.

questions.stem: Calculate the work done when $1$ mole of an ideal gas is expanded reversibly and isothermally from initial pressure $10$ bar to final pressure $1$ bar at constant temperature $300$ K. $[R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the formula
For a reversible isothermal expansion, $w = -2.303\,nRT\log_{10}\frac{V_2}{V_1}$. At constant $T$, $\frac{V_2}{V_1} = \frac{P_1}{P_2}$.
Step 2: Substitute
$n = 1$, $R = 8.314$, $T = 300$ K, $\frac{P_1}{P_2} = 10$, so $\log 10 = 1$.
$$w = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 1 = -5744\ \mathrm{J}$$
Step 3: Convert
$w = -5.744$ kJ. The negative sign means the gas does work on the surroundings. Option (A).
Final Answer:
Work done is $-5.744$ kJ, option (A).
(A) $-5.744$ kJ
Quick Tip: Use $w = -2.303\,nRT\log\frac{P_1}{P_2}$ for reversible isothermal expansion.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes exhibits, $\Delta U = 0$?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the concept
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, $\Delta U = nC_V\Delta T$.
Step 2: Check each process
(A) Adiabatic: $q = 0$ but $\Delta U = w \neq 0$.
(B) Isothermal: $\Delta T = 0$ so $\Delta U = 0$.
(C) Isobaric: $T$ changes, so $\Delta U \neq 0$.
(D) Isochoric: $w = 0$ but $\Delta U = q \neq 0$.
Final Answer:
Isothermal process gives $\Delta U = 0$, option (B).
(B)
Quick Tip: For an ideal gas $\Delta U$ depends only on temperature.

questions.stem: Which of the following aqueous solution of salt have $pH < 7$ at 298 K?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Classify each salt
(A) $\mathrm{KNO_3}$: strong base + strong acid, neutral, $pH = 7$.
(B) $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$: strong base + weak acid, basic, $pH > 7$.
(C) $\mathrm{CH_3COONH_4}$: weak acid + weak base with nearly equal strengths, about neutral.
(D) $\mathrm{CuCl_2}$: weak base $\mathrm{Cu(OH)_2}$ + strong acid HCl, acidic.
Step 2: Reason for (D)
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ hydrolyses: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2H_2O \rightleftharpoons Cu(OH)_2 + 2H^{+}}$. Extra $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ makes $pH < 7$.
Final Answer:
$\mathrm{CuCl_2}$ solution is acidic, option (D).
(D) $\mathrm{CuCl_2}$
Quick Tip: A salt of a strong acid and a weak base gives an acidic solution.

questions.stem: What happens when solid $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ dissolved in water?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the hydrolysis
$\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid ($\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$). The carbonate ion reacts with water:
$$\mathrm{CO_3^{2-} + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HCO_3^{-} + OH^{-}}$$
Step 2: Read off the result
$[\mathrm{OH^{-}}]$ rises, so the solution is basic, $pH > 7$.
So (A) is right, (B) is wrong because pH changes, (C) is wrong because $[\mathrm{H^{+}}]$ falls, and (D) is wrong because a basic solution turns red litmus blue, not blue litmus red.
Final Answer:
Dissolving $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ raises $[\mathrm{OH^{-}}]$, option (A).
(A)
Quick Tip: Carbonate ion is the anion of a weak acid, so it hydrolyses and releases $\mathrm{OH^{-}}$.

questions.stem:
What happens when $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ is dissolved in water?
Identify correct statements from the following
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify the salt
$\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ comes from the weak base $\mathrm{Cu(OH)_2}$ and the strong acid $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$.
Step 2: Hydrolysis
Only the cation hydrolyses: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2H_2O \rightleftharpoons Cu(OH)_2 + 2H^{+}}$.
This releases $\mathrm{H^{+}}$, so $pH < 7$.
Step 3: Check options
(A) is false, since the anion $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ does not react (it is the conjugate base of a strong acid).
(B) is false, an acidic solution turns blue litmus red.
(C) is true.
(D) is false, since the salt does hydrolyse.
Final Answer:
$\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ solution has pH below $7$, option (C).
(C)
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ is a salt of a weak base and a strong acid, so the solution is acidic.

options.text: Anion of the salt react with water.
Its solution will turn red litmus into blue.
The pH of the solution will be less than $7$.
The $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ will not undergo hydrolysis reaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is obtained when dihydrogen reacts with the alkali metals at high temperature?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the reaction
At high temperature, dihydrogen combines with alkali metals to give ionic hydrides:
$$\mathrm{2M + H_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2MH}$$
Step 2: Check
Alkoxides need an alcohol. Peroxides form with oxygen. Nitrites need nitrogen and oxygen. So only metal hydrides fit, option (B).
Final Answer:
The product is a metal hydride, option (B).
(B)
Quick Tip: Hydrogen takes an electron from the alkali metal to form $\mathrm{H^{-}}$.

questions.stem: What type of isomerism is exhibited by neopentane?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify the compound
Neopentane is 2,2-dimethylpropane, $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$.
Step 2: Find the isomer relation
$\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$ has three structures: n-pentane, isopentane and neopentane. They differ only in the chain of carbon atoms, so this is chain isomerism.
Step 3: Others
Position isomerism needs a movable substituent or double bond. Geometrical isomerism needs a double bond or ring. Tautomerism needs a labile hydrogen with a carbonyl-like group. None applies.
Final Answer:
Neopentane shows chain isomerism, option (B).
(B) chain

questions.stem: Which from following is obtained as major product when methoxybenzene is treated with nitrating mixture?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify the directing group
The methoxy group donates electrons by resonance, so it activates the ring and directs to ortho and para.
Step 2: Nitration
With $\mathrm{HNO_3/H_2SO_4}$ the electrophile is $\mathrm{NO_2^{+}}$. It attacks the ortho and para positions.
Step 3: Major product
The para product is major because the ortho positions are hindered by the $\mathrm{OCH_3}$ group. So the major product is 4-nitroanisole. Nitrophenols are wrong because the ether group is not cleaved under these conditions.
Final Answer:
The major product is 4-nitroanisole, option (B).
(B)
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$ is an ortho/para director and para is favoured by sterics.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is carcinogenic and toxic?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the facts
Benzene is a toxic liquid and a known carcinogen. Long exposure damages bone marrow and can cause leukaemia.
Step 2: Others
Simple alkanes, alkenes and alkynes are not classed as carcinogens in this sense. So option (C).
Final Answer:
Benzene is carcinogenic and toxic, option (C).
(C)
Quick Tip: Benzene is a known human carcinogen.

questions.stem: Pt has FCC structure with an edge length of unit cell $392$ pm. What is the radius of Pt?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Use FCC geometry
In an FCC cell, atoms touch along the face diagonal. The face diagonal is $\sqrt{2}a$ and holds $4r$.
$$4r = \sqrt{2}\,a \ \Rightarrow\ r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$$
Step 2: Substitute
$$r = \frac{392}{2 \times 1.414} = \frac{392}{2.828} = 138.6\ \mathrm{pm}$$
Step 3: Check
The value $196$ pm would be $a/2$, which applies to a simple cubic cell, not FCC. So option (A).
Final Answer:
$r = 138.6$ pm, option (A).
(A) $138.6$ pm
Quick Tip: In FCC the face diagonal is $4r$, so $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.stem:
In a cubic unit cell of an ionic compound, the eight corners are occupied by anions and cations at the center of the cube. Calculate the volume of the unit cell if density of the unit cell is $4\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.
[Molar mass of compound $= 168.6\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ and $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Step 1: Count formula units
Anions at 8 corners give $8 \times \frac{1}{8} = 1$ anion. One cation at the centre. So the cell holds $Z = 1$ formula unit (like $\mathrm{CsCl}$).
Step 2: Use the density formula
$$\rho = \frac{ZM}{N_A V} \ \Rightarrow\ V = \frac{ZM}{\rho N_A}$$
Step 3: Substitute
$$V = \frac{1 \times 168.6}{4 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}} = \frac{168.6}{2.409 \times 10^{24}} = 7.0 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$$
Step 4: Check
If one used $Z = 2$ the answer would double, which is not an option. So option (C).
Final Answer:
$V = 7.0 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, option (C).
(C)
Quick Tip: Count $Z$ first: corners give $8 \times \frac{1}{8} = 1$ anion, center gives $1$ cation.

questions.stem: What is the total number of spheres that surrounds the tetrahedral hole in the close-packed three-dimensional structure?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Define the hole
A tetrahedral hole is formed when one sphere sits in the depression of three spheres in a layer, with a fourth sphere on top.
Step 2: Count
Three spheres in the lower layer plus one above gives $4$ spheres whose centres form a tetrahedron. Octahedral holes have $6$ neighbours instead. Option (B).
Final Answer:
A tetrahedral hole has $4$ surrounding spheres, option (B).
(B)
Quick Tip: A tetrahedral void sits among $4$ touching spheres.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a green alternative for dry cleaning solvents?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall green chemistry
Dry cleaning used tetrachloroethene (perchloroethylene) and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$, which are toxic and pollute groundwater. Benzene is carcinogenic.
Step 2: Alternative
Liquid or supercritical $\mathrm{CO_2}$ with a detergent is non-toxic, recyclable and leaves no harmful waste. Option (D).
Final Answer:
Supercritical $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is the green solvent, option (D).
(D)
Quick Tip: The green choice is non-toxic and recyclable: supercritical carbon dioxide.

questions.stem:
Vapour pressure of $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ at $25^\circ$C is $143$ mm Hg. If $0.5$ g of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in $100\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $\mathrm{CCl_4}$. Find the vapour pressure of the solution.
(Density of $\mathrm{CCl_4} = 1.58\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$ and molecular weight of solute is $65$)
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find the moles
Mass of $\mathrm{CCl_4} = 100 \times 1.58 = 158$ g. Molar mass of $\mathrm{CCl_4} = 154$, so $n_{\text{solvent}} = \frac{158}{154} = 1.026$ mol.
Moles of solute $= \frac{0.5}{65} = 0.00769$ mol.
Step 2: Mole fraction of solute
$$x_2 = \frac{0.00769}{0.00769 + 1.026} = 0.00744$$
Step 3: Lowering of vapour pressure
$$P^0 - P = 0.00744 \times 143 = 1.064\ \mathrm{mm}$$
$$P = 143 - 1.064 = 141.93\ \mathrm{mm}$$
Step 4: Check
Other options exceed $143$ mm, which is impossible since a solute lowers the pressure. Option (A).
Final Answer:
The vapour pressure is $141.93$ mm Hg, option (A).
(A)
Quick Tip: Use Raoult's law: $\frac{P^0 - P}{P^0} = x_{\text{solute}}$.

questions.stem: The solubility of $\mathrm{N_2}$ gas in water at $25^\circ$C and $1$ bar is $6.85 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$. Calculate the solubility of $\mathrm{N_2}$ gas in water at the same temperature when the partial pressure of $\mathrm{N_2}$ is $0.70$ bar
questions.solution:
Step 1: State Henry's law
The solubility of a gas is directly proportional to its partial pressure: $S \propto p$.
Step 2: Compute
$$S_2 = 6.85 \times 10^{-4} \times \frac{0.70}{1} = 4.795 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$$
Step 3: Result
Option (C).
Final Answer:
Solubility is $4.795 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$, option (C).
(C)
Quick Tip: Henry's law: solubility is directly proportional to partial pressure.

questions.stem:
Identify from the following pair of solutions that exhibits the same osmotic pressure.
[molar mass of urea $= 60\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ and molar mass of glucose $= 180\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
Step 1: Use $\pi = CRT$
Osmotic pressure depends on molarity at the same $T$. Urea and glucose do not ionise, so only molarity matters.
Step 2: Compute molarities
(A) Urea $\frac{6}{60} = 0.1$ M, glucose $\frac{18}{180} = 0.1$ M. Equal.
(B) $0.2$ M vs $0.1$ M. Not equal.
(C) $0.3$ M vs $0.1$ M. Not equal.
(D) $0.1$ M vs $0.033$ M. Not equal.
Final Answer:
Both solutions in (A) are $0.1$ M, option (A).
(A)
Quick Tip: Equal molar concentrations of non-electrolytes give equal osmotic pressure.

options.text: $6$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$12$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$18$ g/L urea solution and $18$ g/L glucose solution.
$6$ g/L urea solution and $6$ g/L glucose solution.

questions.stem: At $298$ K, the specific conductance ($\kappa$) of a $0.0020$ M NaCl solution is $2.50 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}$. Calculate the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of the solution in $\mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}$.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the formula
Molar conductivity links to specific conductance by $\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{M}$, where $M$ is the molarity and the factor $1000$ converts $\mathrm{cm^3}$ to litres.
Step 2: Substitute
$$\Lambda_m = \frac{2.50 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.0020} = \frac{0.25}{0.0020} = 125\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}$$
Step 3: Check the options
$62.5$ comes from using $0.004$ M, $12.5$ from dropping a factor of $10$, and $250$ from using $0.001$ M. The correct value is $125$, option (A).
Final Answer:
$\Lambda_m = 125\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}$, option (A).
(A) $125$
Quick Tip: Use $\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{M}$ with $\kappa$ in $\mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding electrolysis of molten NaCl?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the cell reactions
Molten NaCl contains $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^{-}}$ ions.
Cathode: $\mathrm{Na^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow Na}$ (reduction).
Anode: $\mathrm{2Cl^{-} \rightarrow Cl_2 + 2e^{-}}$ (oxidation).
Step 2: Check the statements
(A) Pale green $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ gas appears at the anode: true.
(B) Silvery white molten sodium forms at the cathode: true.
(C) The overall change is NaCl into Na and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$: also true, but option (D) combines (A) and (B), the two statements the question builds on. So (D) is the answer.
Final Answer:
Both A and B are correct, option (D).
(D)
Quick Tip: Chlorine forms at the anode and sodium at the cathode.

options.text: Pale green $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ gas released at anode
Molten silvery white sodium is deposited at cathode
Decomposition of NaCl into Na metal and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ gas

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the voltaic cell?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the idea
A voltaic (galvanic) cell uses a spontaneous redox reaction to produce an electric current. Chemical energy turns into electrical energy.
Step 2: Check the options
(A) is true.
(B) describes an electrolytic cell, so it is false.
(C) In a voltaic cell the anode is the negative electrode (oxidation releases electrons), so it is false.
(D) The cathode is positive in a voltaic cell, so it is false.
Final Answer:
A voltaic cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy, option (A).
(A)
Quick Tip: A voltaic cell makes electricity from a spontaneous chemical reaction.

options.text: It converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
It converts electrical energy into chemical energy.
The anode of voltaic cells is positive.
The cathode of voltaic cell is negative.

questions.stem: Identify the function of salt bridge.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the role
The salt bridge is a U-tube holding an inert electrolyte such as KCl in agar. It joins the two half cells and lets ions move between them.
Step 2: Why that matters
It completes the electrical circuit and keeps each half cell electrically neutral as ions are made or used. It is not an electrode, so (A) and (B) fail. It cannot measure potential, so (D) fails. Option (C) is correct.
Final Answer:
The salt bridge connects the two half cells, option (C).
Quick Tip: The salt bridge closes the circuit and keeps both solutions neutral.

questions.stem: A first order reaction complete $60\%$ in $20$ minutes. How long will the reaction take to complete $84\%$?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Find $k$
For first order, $k = \frac{2.303}{t}\log\frac{a}{a-x}$. After $60\%$ completion, $a - x = 40$ when $a = 100$.
$$k = \frac{2.303}{20}\log\frac{100}{40} = \frac{2.303 \times 0.3979}{20} = 0.0458\ \mathrm{min^{-1}}$$
Step 2: Time for $84\%$
Now $a - x = 16$.
$$t = \frac{2.303}{0.0458}\log\frac{100}{16} = \frac{2.303 \times 0.7959}{0.0458} = 40\ \mathrm{min}$$
Step 3: Check
Option (C) is $40\ \mathrm{min}$. Others come from assuming linear progress.
Final Answer:
The reaction takes $40\ \mathrm{min}$, option (C).
Quick Tip: Find $k$ from the $60\%$ data, then use $t = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\frac{100}{100-x}$.

questions.stem: The rate constant for a first order reaction is $60\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. How much time will it take to reduce the concentration of the reactant to $1/20^{\mathrm{th}}$ of its initial value?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the integrated law
$$t = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$$
Step 2: Substitute
The concentration falls to $\frac{1}{20}$, so the ratio is $20$ and $\log 20 = 1.301$.
$$t = \frac{2.303 \times 1.301}{60} = \frac{2.996}{60} = 0.0499\ \mathrm{s}$$
Step 3: Result
Option (C), $0.0499\ \mathrm{s}$.
Final Answer:
The time is $0.0499\ \mathrm{s}$, option (C).
Quick Tip: Use $t = \frac{2.303}{k}\log\frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$ with $[A]_0/[A] = 20$.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the rate constant?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the meaning
In the rate law $r = k[A]^{n}$, $k$ is the proportionality constant. It does not depend on concentration but changes with temperature.
Step 2: Check the options
(A), (B) and (C) are true.
(D) is false: for the same concentrations a larger $k$ gives a larger rate, so the reaction is faster.
Final Answer:
Statement (D) is not true, option (D).
Quick Tip: A larger rate constant means a faster reaction, not a slower one.

options.text: It is proportionality constant in rate law that relates reaction rate to reactant concentrations.
It is independent of concentration of reactant.
Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following assertions about the extent of physisorption is correct?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the facts
Physisorption is caused by weak Van der Waals forces and is exothermic.
Step 2: Check the options
(A) False. By Le Chatelier, raising temperature opposes an exothermic process.
(B) False. A larger surface area increases adsorption.
(C) False. Stronger Van der Waals forces increase adsorption.
(D) True.
Final Answer:
Physisorption decreases with temperature, option (D).
Quick Tip: Physisorption is exothermic, so it falls as temperature rises.

options.text: Decreases with increase in surface area
Decreases with increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces

questions.stem: Which of the following is not characteristics of interhalogen compounds?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the properties
Interhalogen compounds are covalent, volatile solids or liquids. They are not explosive, though they are reactive. They add across $\mathrm{C{=}C}$ bonds of unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Step 2: Find the odd one out
They are strong oxidising agents because the halogen in the positive oxidation state readily takes electrons. So (D) is not a characteristic.
Final Answer:
They are strong oxidising agents, so option (D) is not a characteristic.
Quick Tip: Interhalogens are oxidising agents, not reducing agents.

options.text: Form addition products with unsaturated hydrocarbons.

questions.stem: Identify the set of paramagnetic ions among the following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write configurations
$\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$: $3d^{2}$ (2 unpaired). $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$: $3d^{9}$ (1 unpaired). $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$: $3d^{4}$ (4 unpaired).
Step 2: Check the other sets
(A) has $\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$ ($3d^{0}$), which is diamagnetic.
(B) has $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ ($3d^{10}$), which is diamagnetic.
(D) has $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ ($3d^{0}$), which is diamagnetic.
Only (C) has all three paramagnetic.
Final Answer:
All ions in set (C) have unpaired electrons, option (C).
Quick Tip: Paramagnetic ions have at least one unpaired d electron.

questions.stem: Why zinc does not exhibit variable oxidation states?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the configuration
Zn is $\mathrm{[Ar]}3d^{10}4s^{2}$.
Step 2: Reason
The $3d$ subshell is completely filled and very stable. Zinc loses only its two $4s$ electrons to form $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ and does not disturb the $3d^{10}$ set. So it shows only the $+2$ state.
The $4s$ subshell is also full, but the full $3d$ shell is the reason given. Option (B).
Final Answer:
Zinc has a completely filled $3d$ subshell, option (B).
Quick Tip: Zinc has a stable $3d^{10}$ configuration.

questions.stem: Identify the hybridization in central metal of $\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_5]}$ complex.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Configuration of Fe
Fe has $3d^{6}4s^{2}$. CO is a strong field ligand, so the electrons rearrange to $3d^{8}$, with the $4s^{2}$ electrons pushed into $3d$.
Step 2: Hybrid orbitals
Five CO ligands need five empty orbitals: one $3d$, one $4s$ and three $4p$. This is $dsp^{3}$ hybridisation.
The shape is trigonal bipyramidal.
Step 3: Other options
$sp^{3}d^{2}$ and $d^{2}sp^{3}$ would give six ligands. $sp^{3}$ would give four. Option (A).
Final Answer:
Fe in $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$ is $dsp^{3}$ hybridised, option (A).
Quick Tip: Fe in $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$ is $3d^{8}4s^{0}$ after pairing electrons, giving $dsp^{3}$.

questions.stem: In a complex compound, central metal ion is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the bonding
Ligands donate lone pairs to the central metal ion through coordinate bonds.
Step 2: Name the role
The species that accepts an electron pair is a Lewis acid, so the central metal ion is a Lewis acid. The ligands are Lewis bases. Option (C).
Final Answer:
The metal ion is a Lewis acid, option (C).
Quick Tip: The central metal ion accepts lone pairs from ligands.

questions.stem: Which one of the following factors proceeds more rapidly, unimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism
$\mathrm{S_N1}$ is a two-step reaction. The slow step is ionisation to a carbocation, so the rate depends only on the substrate.
Step 2: Which factor helps
A polar protic solvent solvates the carbocation and the leaving group, so it speeds up the slow step. Nucleophile strength does not change the rate. Aprotic solvents favour $\mathrm{S_N2}$. Option (D).
Final Answer:
A polar protic solvent speeds up $\mathrm{S_N1}$, option (D).
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{S_N1}$ goes through a carbocation, which polar protic solvents stabilise.

questions.stem: Wurtz reaction is NOT possible with
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the reaction
The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether: $\mathrm{2RX + 2Na \rightarrow R{-}R + 2NaX}$.
Step 2: Which halide fails
Tertiary halides such as $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCl}$ mainly undergo elimination to give alkenes, because the strongly basic alkyl sodium removes a $\beta$-hydrogen.
Primary halides (B, C) work well, and the secondary halide (D) can also couple. So (A) is correct.
Final Answer:
Wurtz reaction fails for the tertiary halide, option (A).
Quick Tip: Tertiary halides eliminate instead of coupling.

questions.stem: The major product 'B' in the below mentioned reaction is-
questions.solution:
Step 1: Understanding the Figure:
The reactant is 2-bromopropane, $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3}$. It is heated with alcoholic KOH to give compound A. Then A reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide to give B.
Step 2: Step A: Elimination:
Alcoholic KOH removes HBr from an alkyl halide (dehydrohalogenation). The H comes from a carbon next to the one holding Br.
$$\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{Alc.\ KOH,\Delta} CH_3-CH=CH_2 + KBr + H_2O}$$
So A is propene.
Step 3: Step B: Addition of HBr:
Without peroxide, HBr adds by Markovnikov's rule. The hydrogen goes to the double-bond carbon that already has more hydrogens (the terminal $\mathrm{CH_2}$). The bromine goes to the middle carbon, which gives the more stable secondary carbocation.
$$\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2 + HBr \rightarrow CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3}$$
Step 4: Name of B:
B is $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3}$, which is 2-bromopropane.
Step 5: Why the other options are wrong:
1-Bromopropane would form only by anti-Markovnikov addition, which needs peroxide. Bromoethane has only two carbons and carbon tetrabromide has no chain, so neither can form from a three-carbon alkene.
Final Answer:
The major product B is 2-bromopropane, option (C).
Quick Tip: Alcoholic KOH gives propene, and HBr without peroxide adds as per Markovnikov to give back 2-bromopropane.

questions.stem: Which from following is a suitable method for preparation of ether?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the method
In the Williamson synthesis an alkoxide attacks an alkyl halide by an $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reaction. A tertiary halide would eliminate to alkene.
Step 2: Check the options
(A) Tertiary butyl bromide with methoxide gives isobutene by elimination, so it is unsuitable.
(B) Sodium tert-butoxide with methyl bromide gives methyl tert-butyl ether, which is suitable.
(C) Methyl alcohol and ethene do not form an ether this way.
(D) Methyl alcohol and methyl bromide do not react without a base.
Final Answer:
Sodium tert-butoxide and methyl bromide work, option (B).
Quick Tip: Williamson synthesis needs a primary alkyl halide and an alkoxide.

questions.stem: The molecule with a maximum boiling point is
questions.solution:
Step 1: Compare intermolecular forces
Compound (A) is butane-1,3-diol with two OH groups, so it forms strong hydrogen bonds in many directions.
(B) and (C) are alkyl bromides with only dipole and dispersion forces.
(D) has one OH group and a smaller molar mass.
Step 2: Decide
Two OH groups give the strongest hydrogen bonding, so (A) has the highest boiling point.
Final Answer:
The diol (A) has the highest boiling point.
Quick Tip: Hydrogen bonding raises the boiling point most, and a diol has two OH groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following reactions is an example of a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the definition
Disproportionation means one species is oxidised and reduced at the same time.
Step 2: Check the reactions
Wolff-Kishner and Clemmensen are reductions of carbonyl to $\mathrm{CH_2}$.
Aldol condensation forms a C-C bond.
In the Cannizzaro reaction, two molecules of an aldehyde with no alpha hydrogen give an alcohol (reduction) and an acid salt (oxidation). So (D).
Final Answer:
Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation, option (D).
Quick Tip: In a disproportionation, the same species is both oxidised and reduced.

questions.stem: Acetaldehyde, when heated in the presence of sodium hydroxide and iodine forms
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recognise the test
Compounds with a $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ group give the iodoform reaction with $\mathrm{I_2}$ and NaOH.
Step 2: Write the reaction
$$\mathrm{CH_3CHO + 3I_2 + 4NaOH \rightarrow CHI_3 + HCOONa + 3NaI + 3H_2O}$$
Step 3: Result
The salt formed is sodium formate. Option (A).
Final Answer:
The product salt is sodium formate, option (A).
Quick Tip: This is the iodoform reaction: $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ gives $\mathrm{CHI_3}$ and sodium formate.

questions.stem: Identify the product obtained when Grignard reagent reacts with alkyl cyanide followed by acid hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Write the reaction
$$\mathrm{R'MgX + RC \equiv N \rightarrow RC(=NMgX)R' \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} RCOR'}$$
Step 2: Result
The imine intermediate hydrolyses to a ketone. Option (B).
Final Answer:
A ketone is obtained, option (B).
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{RMgX}$ adds to the $\mathrm{C{\equiv}N}$ triple bond, and hydrolysis gives a ketone.

questions.stem: Which of following amines exhibits carbylamine test?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the test
In the carbylamine test, a primary amine is heated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH to give a foul-smelling isocyanide.
Step 2: Conclude
It needs two N-H bonds to lose, so secondary and tertiary amines do not respond. Option (C).
Final Answer:
Primary amines respond, option (C).
Quick Tip: Only primary amines form isocyanides with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and KOH.

questions.stem: Identify the product obtained when $\mathrm{RCN}$ is treated with sodium and alcohol.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the reaction
Sodium with alcohol is a reducing mixture (nascent hydrogen). It reduces $\mathrm{R{-}C \equiv N}$ to $\mathrm{RCH_2NH_2}$.
Step 2: Result
The amine has one more carbon than R. Option (C).
Final Answer:
The product is $\mathrm{RCH_2NH_2}$, option (C).
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{Na/C_2H_5OH}$ reduces a nitrile to a primary amine.

questions.stem: The reaction of glucose with acetic Anhydride, confirms the
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the reaction
Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to give glucose pentaacetate.
Step 2: Meaning
Five acetyl groups attach, one on each hydroxyl group, so glucose has five OH groups. Option (D).
Final Answer:
It confirms five hydroxyl groups, option (D).
Quick Tip: Five acetyl groups attach, so there are five OH groups.

questions.stem: The secondary structure of protein is determined by
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the structures
The secondary structure is the alpha helix or beta pleated sheet.
Step 2: Reason
They are held in shape by hydrogen bonds between the $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ and $\mathrm{N{-}H}$ groups of the peptide backbone. Option (D).
Final Answer:
Hydrogen bonds decide the secondary structure, option (D).
Quick Tip: Alpha helix and beta sheet are held by hydrogen bonds.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds are used to obtain terylene polymer?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the monomers
Terylene (Dacron, PET) is a polyester from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid).
Step 2: Check
Isophthalic acid (1,3) and phthalic acid (1,2) give other polymers, and propane-1,2-diol is not used. Option (C).
Final Answer:
Ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid, option (C).
Quick Tip: Terylene is made from ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following polymers is also called as dacron?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the names
Terylene, Dacron and PET are the same polyester.
Step 2: Others
Teflon is PTFE, PVC is polyvinyl chloride and Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin. Option (D).
Final Answer:
Terylene is Dacron, option (D).
Quick Tip: Dacron is another name for terylene.

questions.stem: What type of drug the aspirin is?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Recall the use
Aspirin relieves pain and reduces fever and also thins blood. It belongs to the non-narcotic analgesics.
Step 2: Others
It does not kill microbes, so it is not an antimicrobial or antibiotic, and it is not an anti-oxidant. Option (A).
Final Answer:
Aspirin is an analgesic, option (A).
Quick Tip: Aspirin relieves pain.
